findings.title: methods-report: per-method filter+sort of full universe run 3x (top-N, leaderboard, deep-dive)
findings.description: renderHTML does three independent O(M*N*logN) sweeps over the full row set. (1) Top-N-per-Method (line 233-244): for each of ~83 methods it runs discoveryRows.filter(...).sort(...) over all N rows. (2) Kennzahl-Rangliste (line 525-532): for each of 12 LEADERBOARD_METRICS it runs rows.filter(...).map(...).sort(...) over all N rows. (3) deepDiveLists (line 263-269): 5 more full filter+sort sweeps. Each .sort() reaches into r.results[m.id].value via accessor closures, so the comparator re-walks the object on every comparison.
findings.mechanism: M methods x N rows x log(N) comparisons, each comparison dereferencing nested result objects. At N=3528 today the method sweep is ~83 * 3528 * 12 ~ 3.5M comparisons; at the projected 19k universe it is ~83*19000*14 ~ 22M comparisons just for sweep (1), repeated structurally in (2) and (3).
findings.reproducer: node generate-methods-report.js --snapshots ./snapshots ; time the renderHTML phase vs evaluate phase with --prof.
findings.impact: est. seconds-to-low-minutes per report run at full universe; grows superlinearly. Repeated nested dereference in comparators adds constant-factor cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-extract a flat numeric column per metric once (e.g. for each row store row._lb[metricId]=value), then sort plain {ticker,val} tuples. Compute discoveryRows' per-method valid lists in a single forward pass that buckets values per method, then sort each bucket once.

findings.title: modes-report main() recomputes eligibleForMode + topAllMust for every mode just to log counts
findings.description: buildHtml() already computes eligibleByMode[m]=eligibleForMode(evaluated,m) for all modes (line 547) and topAllMust per mode internally. After buildHtml returns, main() loops over every mode AGAIN calling eligibleForMode(evaluated, modeId) (full N-pass filter) and topAllMust(eligible, modeId, topN) (full filter+sort) purely to console.log eligible/all-MUST-pass counts. This duplicates the most expensive per-mode work for output that is already derivable.
findings.mechanism: eligibleForMode is O(N) with a dataGuard loop + sector regex per stock; called modes (4) extra times over N~5-15k stocks. topAllMust adds another O(N*logN) sort per mode. All redundant with buildHtml's internal computation.
findings.reproducer: Add a counter inside eligibleForMode; run modes-report; observe it is invoked 2x per mode (once in buildHtml, once in the logging loop).
findings.impact: est. doubles the per-mode eligibility+sort cost; a few seconds at full universe, pure waste.
findings.suggested_fix: Have buildHtml return (or stash) the per-mode eligible counts and all-MUST-pass counts it already computed, and log those instead of recomputing. Or compute the log line inside buildHtml.

findings.title: modes-report: topAllMust(...,9999).length sorts entire passing set only to count it
findings.description: Within a single render, each mode's eligible set is filtered+sorted several times: topByScore (line 428) sorts by score; blockedByOneMust (line 455) re-scans the same eligible set; topAllMust is invoked with topN=9999 at line 554-555 for HG and QC just to obtain a .length count, forcing a full filter+sort whose sorted result is discarded except for the length. The score accessor a.modeEvals[modeId].score is read repeatedly inside comparators.
findings.mechanism: Per mode: topByScore O(N*logN) + blockedByOneMust O(N) + (for HG,QC) topAllMust O(N*logN) with topN=9999 sorting the entire passing set only to count it.
findings.reproducer: Instrument topAllMust call count; note the 9999-topN calls at line 554-555 produce a sorted array of which only .length is used.
findings.impact: est. low seconds at full universe; the 9999-topN count calls are avoidable sorts.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace topAllMust(...,9999).length with a plain filter().length (no sort needed for a count). Cache modeEvals[modeId].score into a local before sorting to avoid repeated property chains.

findings.title: methods-report: discoveryRows DataGuard filter walks Object.entries(results) per row
findings.description: discoveryRows = rows.filter(r => { for (const [mid,res] of Object.entries(r.results)) { if (MT_local.isDataGuard(mid) && res.computable && res.pass===false) return false } ... }). Object.entries materializes a [k,v] array of all ~83 method results for every one of N rows, and MT_local.isDataGuard(mid) is called for every method even though only a handful are DataGuards. This runs once but is O(N*M) with per-pair allocation.
findings.mechanism: N rows x M methods, each iteration allocating a 2-element entry array and calling isDataGuard. At 19k x 83 ~ 1.6M isDataGuard calls + entry allocations.
findings.reproducer: Profile renderHTML; the discoveryRows filter shows up as an allocation hotspot under --prof.
findings.impact: est. sub-second to ~1s at full universe; mainly GC pressure from Object.entries allocations.
findings.suggested_fix: Precompute the DataGuard method-id list once (MT.dataGuardIds), then for each row iterate only that small list: for (const mid of dataGuardIds) { const res=r.results[mid]; if (res && res.computable && res.pass===false) return false }. Avoids Object.entries and the per-method isDataGuard call.

findings.title: methods-report: snapshot load uses serial blocking readFileSync loop (not migrated to async batches)
findings.description: evaluateAllStocks reads + JSON.parse's every snapshot file synchronously (line 76, fs.readFileSync inside the for-file loop) for all N stocks. modes-report (loadStocks, 32-way) and snapshot-methods-history (loadFilesAsync, 200-batch) were both migrated to fs.promises.readFile batched concurrency; methods-report's loader was NOT and still blocks the event loop serially.
findings.mechanism: Serial fs.readFileSync over N files blocks the event loop; each parse of a multi-KB snapshot is sequential with no I/O overlap.
findings.reproducer: Compare wall-time of the load phase in generate-methods-report.js vs generate-modes-report.js on the same snapshots dir.
findings.impact: est. 1-3 min of serial I/O at 15k+ files (same magnitude the modes/history loaders eliminated by going async).
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the loadStocks() batched fs.promises.readFile pattern (CONCURRENCY=32) from generate-modes-report.js for the snapshot read in evaluateAllStocks; keep evaluate synchronous but parallelize the file reads.

findings.title: methods-report: methodSummary forward pass does lazy-init branch per row*method pair
findings.description: The single-pass method-summary (a prior F-222a fix) iterates for (const r of rows) { for (const m of methods) { ... r.results[m.id] } }. O(N*M) is unavoidable for the summary, but the inner loop indexes _methodCounts[m.id] with a `|| (assign)` lazy-init on every pair rather than pre-initializing the counts map once.
findings.mechanism: N*M iterations each doing `_methodCounts[m.id] || (_methodCounts[m.id] = {...})`; after the first row the `||` always short-circuits but still does a property read + truthiness check per pair.
findings.reproducer: Micro-benchmark the methodSummary block; negligible vs F-PF-001 but measurable.
findings.impact: est. sub-second; included for completeness, low priority.
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-initialize _methodCounts[m.id]={computable:0,passing:0} once before the rows loop, then the inner loop is a plain increment with no lazy-init branch.

findings.title: pull-yahoo reads each snapshot header twice (sortByStaleness + _getExistingSnapshotAge), 4 syscalls each
findings.description: sortByStaleness precomputes an age Map (already an improvement over the prior in-comparator probe). But per ticker it does fs.existsSync THEN fs.openSync/readSync/closeSync — existsSync is a redundant stat before the open. _getExistingSnapshotAge (line 1394) then repeats the SAME 4-syscall header probe per ticker during processOne, so each ticker's snapshot header is read from disk twice per run.
findings.mechanism: existsSync(stat)+openSync+readSync+closeSync = 4 blocking syscalls/ticker in sortByStaleness, plus the same again in _getExistingSnapshotAge. The asOf header is read twice. ~120k blocking syscalls at 15k tickers.
findings.reproducer: Process Monitor the pull start; count open() on snapshots/*.json before first HTTP call then again during processing.
findings.impact: est. a few seconds of blocking syscall time at 15k tickers; doubled by the second probe. Minor vs network time but pure event-loop blocking.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop existsSync and rely on openSync throwing ENOENT (already caught). Have sortByStaleness stash the parsed asOf age into a Map keyed by ticker and pass it to processOne so _getExistingSnapshotAge reuses it instead of re-reading.

findings.title: sector-medians CLI loads all snapshots with serial readFileSync loop
findings.description: The require.main CLI block reads every snapshot via a synchronous for-loop of JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...)). This is the same serial-blocking pattern that modes-report and snapshot-methods-history already replaced with async batched reads. computeMedians itself is a single O(N) pass (good), but the load is serial.
findings.mechanism: Serial fs.readFileSync over N snapshot files blocks the event loop; no parallel I/O.
findings.reproducer: node methods/sector-medians-compute.js ./snapshots and time the read phase vs compute phase.
findings.impact: est. 1-3 min serial I/O at full universe when run as the 'Compute Sector-Medians (auto)' workflow step.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the batched fs.promises.readFile loader (CONCURRENCY 32) used by generate-modes-report.js loadStocks; make the CLI block async.

findings.title: wrapEvaluate + effectiveThreshold re-classify same stock M times per evaluateStock (no sub-profile memo)
findings.description: Runner.evaluateStock calls H.wrapEvaluate for every method on every stock. effectiveThreshold (called inside the individual method.evaluate's) runs classifySubProfile(stock) per method, so the same stock is re-classified up to M times within one evaluateStock — there is no per-stock memo of the sub-profile. Additionally wrapEvaluate runs _dataAsOfFromStock (builds+filters a 4-element candidates array) and _dataAgeDays (Date.parse) on every method*stock pair even though both depend only on the stock, not the method.
findings.mechanism: classifySubProfile(stock) (an engine call) invoked once per threshold-using method, i.e. up to M times for one stock, with no memoization keyed on the stock. wrapEvaluate allocates candidates[] + flags[] arrays per pair. This path runs in methods-report, modes-report, snapshot-methods-history AND pull — the highest-multiplicity hot path in the repo.
findings.reproducer: Add a call counter to classifySubProfile in engine-v7.3; run Runner.evaluateStock on one stock; observe it is called once per threshold-using method rather than once for the stock.
findings.impact: est. potentially the dominant CPU cost of every report/history run after I/O; memoizing sub-profile per stock and hoisting dataAsOf/ageDays could cut a large fraction of per-method overhead. Quantify with --prof (classifySubProfile self-time).
findings.suggested_fix: Memoize classifySubProfile on the stock (stock.__sp) for the duration of one evaluateStock, or pass the computed sub-profile into effectiveThreshold. Hoist _dataAsOfFromStock/_dataAgeDays to once-per-stock and pass ageDays into wrapEvaluate.

findings.title: modes-report dedupeByCompany norm() runs ~5 full-string regex scans per stock name
findings.description: dedupeByCompany.norm() applies chained .replace() calls (3 accent classes + suffix regex + non-alnum) to every stock name. The accent replaces use character-class regexes that scan the whole string each time. Runs once per evaluated stock so O(N) with ~5 regex scans each. The suffix regex is correctly hoisted to module scope (prior F-PF-011 fix), but the accent regexes are re-created as literals each call.
findings.mechanism: N stocks x ~5 full-string regex scans. Minor vs evaluate cost but a tight per-stock loop.
findings.reproducer: Profile dedupeByCompany; norm self-time scales with universe size.
findings.impact: est. sub-second at full universe; low priority.
findings.suggested_fix: Combine the three accent-class replaces into a single replace with a lookup map, or normalize via String.prototype.normalize('NFD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g,'') once. Fast-path pure-ASCII names to skip normalization.
